key_insight: The paper introduces an auditable workflow that combines LLM assistance, deterministic checks, and human oversight to produce versioned evidence syntheses with traceable corrections.
clinical_relevance: This could make LLM-assisted systematic reviews more transparent and trustworthy for clinical evidence generation, though it is not yet shown to improve patient outcomes.
method: LLM agents interpreted sources and extracted review data.
Deterministic code enforced statistical rules and tracked corrections.
Investigators resolved ambiguities and authorized final release of the synthesis.
evidence_signal: In a retrospective test of one registered prognostic review, the system documented 50 root-cause events, corrected most of them, and achieved byte-identical agreement across release and publication packages.
watch_item: This is a single-case retrospective evaluation without an external comparator, so generalizability and real-world benefit remain unproven.
paper_title: An auditable evidence compiler for large language model-assisted systematic reviews
